title: What is known about 1RB1RF_1LC1RE_0LD0LC_1RD0RB_1RA0RB_1RC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RF_1LC1RE_0LD0LC_1RD0RB_1RA0RB_1RC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is a word of blocks of 1s on the left and a binary counter on the right; the head rewrites the word by a fixed map and counts. This page lists what has been established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean (kernel) proves the six regular macro steps and the two main shapes of the anomaly for all parameter values, and no halt in the first 10,000 steps (107 with native_decide). Lean also shows that the pattern of the word and of the gaps is not an invariant by itself: a short Q configuration of the same form halts after 190 steps. Non-halting therefore depends on sizes: every collision cascade must end before the word runs out. In the simulated run it is always won, by at least 8.0 bits. Update, 12 November. Lean now also proves this machine's own form of the anomaly with a one-unit counter, 20 collision rules, and a partial macro map (a function from one word-and-counter configuration to the next, proved to be followed by the machine wherever it is defined). The map is far from complete: of the 236 collisions in the simulated run, 187 follow a proved rule. For the sister machine 1RB0RF_1LC1RE_0LD0LC_1RD0RB_1RA0RB_0LC--- the map is complete; here the collisions have many more cases, and they keep a misaligned gap alive instead of clearing it.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: The six regular Q-steps
claims.text: From W 0 1^(3a) B>0 R the machine reaches the next Q configuration after a step count linear in the parameters, in each of the six cases (last block 2j+5, 3, or a 1 after 2i+1; counter low part a+2, or one unit then t gaps of 2): shift rules generated by bbtools.symtm.prove.

claims.title: Q-step = φ twice, counter plus one
claims.text: The same six steps restated on Q configurations qc W a P T: the word goes to phi (phi W) (phi defined on lists) and the counter's low part and gaps update as a binary counter.

claims.title: The anomaly, exactly
claims.text: When the word has run out the machine rewrites it in one sweep, for every value of the parameters and every tape beyond: from 1^(2c+2) 0 1^(3(a+1)) B>0 R (blank to the left) it reaches 1^2 (0 1)^c 0 1^3 B>0 0^(3a) 1 R, one cell further left, in 3a+8c+17 steps; from the word 1^(2c+2) 0 1 with a+2 units it reaches the word 2 1…1 3 with a gap of 3a+1 in 3a+8c+46 steps. The new gap is the misaligned one (not of the form 3p+2).

claims.title: The word-and-gap pattern is not an invariant
claims.text: From the Q configuration 1^2 0 1^3 0 1^3 B>0 (a valid word 2 3, a one-unit counter, no gaps, blank tape) the machine halts at step 190. Its word is so short that it runs out a second time before the misaligned gap made by the first anomaly is cleared; the second anomaly leaves gaps of 1 and 0 in a row, and the collision on them halts. So no proof can use only the shape of the word and of the gaps (even/odd blocks, gaps ≡ 2 mod 3): it has to carry the sizes.

claims.title: Pieces of the irregular steps
claims.text: Five rules that hold for all six machines of the family and for every value of the parameters: the head rewrites the end of the word as φ applied twice and comes back, without reading the tape on either side (3 shapes of the word's end); and the way a regular step with a one-unit low part ends (next gap at least 3 cells, or blank tape).

claims.title: The anomaly with a one-unit counter, for this machine
claims.text: Word a block 2c+2 and a single 1, counter low part one unit (4 rules): with no gap of 2 behind, the new word is 2 1…1 5 1 and the next gap (at least 5 cells) loses 5; with one gap of 2 behind, the new word is 2 1…1 5 3 and the next gap (at least 4 cells) loses 4; the same with blank tape. The counter restarts from one unit. This step passes an F event, so it differs between the six machines. These rules are statements about tapes; they are not yet part of the macro map below.

claims.title: Some collisions
claims.text: A collision starts with the counter's low part one unit, then t gaps of length 2, then a misaligned gap of 0 or 1 cells. Ten cases, each with a next gap of at least 5 cells or blank tape (20 rules): misaligned gap 0 with 0, 1, 2 or 3 gaps of 2 behind when t is even and 0, 1 or 2 when t is odd; misaligned gap 1 with at least one gap of 2 behind when t is even (any number) and with 0 or 1 when t is odd. In each the word takes its double step, its last block grows by 2, 3t/2 single 1s and one to four more blocks are appended, and the next gap loses 3, 4 or 5 cells. Proved for every value of the parameters and any tape to the left.

claims.title: A partial macro map
claims.text: A function astep that sends a word-and-counter configuration (word, low part, list of gap lengths) to the next one. It is defined for the regular steps, for the anomaly when the low part is wide enough, and for the collisions above; elsewhere it answers ‘no rule’. Lean proves that wherever it is defined the machine really goes from the first configuration to the second, in at least 17 steps. It does not cover the anomaly with a one-unit counter, and the very first configuration of the run from blank tape (step 27) is one, so this map cannot yet follow the run from the start: it is a building block, not a bound.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 145 cells have been visited and 64 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: A direct C run (c/fevents.c of the family folder) reaches 2·1010 steps; it has 7 F events (A reading 1), each followed by a 0.

claims.title: Accelerated simulator agrees with direct runs
claims.text: py/hyb.py reproduces every F-event time of the direct run up to 2·1010 steps, and 6 direct runs of 3·108 steps from random mid-phase Q events end where it predicts (for the first machine of the family, also 64,065 consecutive Q events of one phase and 11 more mid-phase checks).

claims.title: 300 transients without a halt
claims.text: The accelerated simulator runs 300 anomalies and collisions from blank tape, up to about 2<sup>2836</sup> steps and a tape 5664 cells wide, with no halt.

claims.title: Shapes of the irregular phases
claims.text: In 300 transients of the accelerated run: all 236 collisions start with the counter's low part one unit, then only gaps of length 2, then a misaligned gap of length 0 (134) or 1 (102); all 64 anomalies start from the word [x] or [x, 1], never with a misaligned gap pending.

claims.title: The race
claims.text: Over 62 epochs (anomaly to anomaly) the collision cascade ends at most 2<sup>278</sup> steps after the anomaly, while the epoch lasts up to 2<sup>2762</sup> steps; the smallest margin is 8.0 bits (1 epoch below 10 bits).

claims.title: Coverage of the proved rules
claims.text: In 300 anomalies and collisions of the accelerated run from blank tape, 187 of the 236 collisions and all anomalies with a wide low part are instances of the partial macro map, and the map gives exactly the simulated result each time; 49 collisions and the 27 anomalies with a one-unit counter are outside it.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/exp
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.0). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.039).

claims.title: How the other collisions differ
claims.text: With a long next gap the table continues regularly: each further pair of gaps of 2 behind the misaligned gap adds a block of 5 to the word. These rows (a block of 5 repeated) and the cases with a next gap shorter than 5 cells are not proved. Found by simulating each case for a few sizes; not proved.

claims.title: Gap alignment
claims.text: In every run the gaps after the first misaligned gap have length ≡ 2 (mod 3), at least 2. The halting patterns of the collisions that we found need a gap of length 0 there.
claims.where: observed over all simulated transients; not proved

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. What is missing, in order: (1) the remaining collision cases as Lean rules. Unlike in the 0LC machine, a collision here does not clear the misaligned gap: it shortens the next gap by 3 to 7 cells, which is misaligned in turn, so gaps of every small length occur and each needs its own case; in several cases the head also goes back into the word. A finer description (the configurations with an empty low part that follow an F event) would probably replace this case list by a few rules. (2) the one-unit anomaly and those rules inside the macro map, so that it follows the run from step 27. (3) the size argument: every cascade of collisions ends before the word runs out. For the 0LC machine, where (1) and (2) are done, (3) is the open part and looks like a Collatz-type question; the same is to be expected here.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine keeps a word of blocks of 1s on the left and a binary counter on the right, and rewrites the word by a fixed map at every count. The regular steps and the reset of the word are proved in Lean. Whether it halts comes down to a race: the gaps left behind by each reset have to be cleared before the word runs out again.

facts.text: The regular macro steps and the reset of the word, for all parameters.
A short Q configuration of the same form halts: sizes matter.
Smallest margin of the race in 300 simulated transients.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.0). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.039).
After 109 steps the tape spans 145 cells (6 left of the start, 119 right), with a density of 1s of 0.441.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A word and a counter
html: This machine is one of six G12 holdouts that share every transition except two: A1 (0RF or 1RF) and F0. Here A1 is 1RF and F0 is 1RC. Both are used only at an F event, when state A reads a 1, which is rare (see the last section). Everything else is the same for the six machines, and so is this page up to that point.

Most of the time the tape reads W 0 1^(3a) B>0 R. We call this a Q configuration. W is a word: blocks of 1s separated by single 0s, with a blank tape to its left. The first block is even and every later block is odd. R is a run of gaps 0^(3p+2) 1. The run of 3a ones before the head and the gaps together hold a binary counter: a and the gap sizes p are its digits, read in parts. The head stays between the word and the counter. It goes left and rewrites the end of the word, then goes right and adds one to the counter.

On the word the machine applies a fixed map φ. It removes the last block b, adds 2 to the block before it, and appends (b−1)/2 blocks of a single 1. The total width stays the same. Applying it repeatedly, a word with blocks 2 3 1 5 goes like this:

word (blocks)tape
2 3 1 51^2 0 1^3 0 1 0 1^5
2 3 3 1 11^2 0 1^3 0 1^3 0 1 0 1
2 3 3 31^2 0 1^3 0 1^3 0 1^3
2 3 5 11^2 0 1^3 0 1^5 0 1
2 3 71^2 0 1^3 0 1^7

Repeated φ carries every block into the first one: the word eventually becomes a single block. The number of steps this takes is exactly N(W) = Σi≥2 2(Si−1)/2, where Si is the width of the word from block i to the end. So φ is itself a counter, written in a mixed radix.

sections.heading: One Q-step: φ twice, the counter plus one
html: From one Q configuration to the next, the machine applies φ twice to the word and adds one to the counter. The step count is a linear function of the parameters. The step depends only on the last one or two blocks of the word (a last block of 2j+5, a last block of 3, or a last 1 after an odd block) and on the lowest part of the counter (at least two units, or one unit followed by t gaps of length 2). That gives six cases.

word endscountersteps
1^(2j+5)a+2 ≥ 23a + 8j + 41
1^(2j+5)one unit, t short gaps8j + 3t + 41
1^3a+23a + 33
1^3one unit, t3t + 33
1^(2i+1) 0 1a+23a + 8i + 33
1^(2i+1) 0 1one unit, t8i + 3t + 33

All six are Lean theorems checked by the kernel, for every value of the parameters and every tape beyond. lean/Rules.lean states them as shift rules. lean/Macro.lean restates them on Q configurations qc W a P T, with φ defined as a Lean function on lists, for example qstep_big_wide.

sections.heading: Long cycles, anomalies and collisions
html: Between Q events the counter climbs. When it overflows, the run of ones 1^(3k) gets longer by one unit and the counter starts again from zero. A full cycle with counter length k applies φ about 2k times, and each extra unit roughly doubles the time. That is why the right side of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count.

The regular Q-steps break down in two ways, called transients. An anomaly happens when the word has become a single block: φ has nothing left to carry, and the block restarts as 2 1 1 … one cell further left. A collision happens when the counter overflows into a gap that is too short. The accelerated simulator py/hyb.py (in the folder of 1RB0RF_1LC1RE_0LD0LC_1RD0RB_1RA0RB_0LC---) jumps over regular stretches with the closed forms above and runs every transient cell by cell. It agrees with direct simulation on every F event up to 2·1010 steps, and on direct runs of 3·108 steps from Q events picked at random in the middle of phases.
For this machine it ran 300 transients without a halt, up to about 22836 steps, with the tape 5664 cells wide.

sections.heading: The anomaly: the word starts again
html: Each φ moves width into the first block, so after N(W) steps the word is a single block (or a block and a single 1). The next Q-step cannot apply φ and does something else, the anomaly. It is short and exact. The head erases the counter's low part, slides the block one cell to the right through the hole it leaves, and comes back rewriting the block as 1 1 0 1 0 1 …:

beforeaftersteps
1^(2c+2) 0 1^(3a+3) B>0 R1^2 (0 1)^c 0 1^3 B>0 0^(3a) 1 R3a+8c+17
1^(2c+2) 0 1 0 1^(3a+6) B>0 R1^2 (0 1)^c 0 1^3 0 1^3 B>0 0^(3a+1) 1 R3a+8c+46

The new word 2 1 1 … 1 has the same width w, and N(W) = 2(w−2)/2 − 1 for it: it lasts that many φ steps. The counter starts again from one unit. Where the old low part was there is now a gap of 3a or 3a+1 cells. That is not of the form 3p+2: it is the misaligned gap. All of the old counter's gaps are still behind it. These are Lean theorems for every a, c and every tape R (anomaly_one, anomaly_two in lean/Transients.lean). The third shape, a block and a single 1 with a one-unit counter, goes through an F event and depends on A1 and F0, so it is not among them.

As the new counter overflows, the misaligned gap shrinks by 3 each time. When it is down to 0 or 1, the next overflow is a collision. The head carries that part of the counter into the end of the word, and the next old gap, a few cells shorter, becomes the misaligned one. This cascade continues until the old gaps are used up and the counter is aligned again.

sections.heading: A race between the word and the cascade
html: Shape alone does not keep the machine running. Lean checks that the Q configuration 1^2 0 1^3 0 1^3 B>0 halts after 190 steps (qc_short_halts). Its word is valid and its counter is aligned, but the word is so short that it runs out again while the misaligned gap made by the first anomaly is still there. The second anomaly then leaves gaps of 1 and 0 in a row, and the collision on them halts. The real run avoids this only because each cascade ends long before the word runs out.

For this machine the cascade after an anomaly ends at most 2278 steps later. The epoch, from one anomaly to the next, lasts up to 22762 steps. The margin (bits of the epoch minus bits of the cascade) is at least 8.0, and is that small only in the first epochs. A proof would need a bound on the cascade, set by the size of the counter at the anomaly, that stays below the word's N(W).

sections.heading: Where it could stop
html: F is reached only from A reading a 1, and F halts on a 1. So a halt needs A to read 1 1. Regular Q-steps never let A read a 1. Only transients do; such a moment is an F event. In the first 2·1010 steps this machine has 7 F events, and at every one the cell after the 1 is a 0.

All the F events we saw happen in collisions. A collision starts when the counter's low part is one unit followed only by gaps of length 2 and then a misaligned gap of length 0 or 1. The head sweeps that part of the counter into the word, and the next gap becomes the misaligned one, shortened by a few cells. A halt needs a gap of length 0 right after such a gap. The gaps behind the misaligned one come from the counter as it was at the anomaly. In every run they have length ≡ 2 (mod 3) and at least 2, so the halt never comes.

Status: open. Lean proves the regular dynamics, the anomaly and that the word-and-gap pattern alone does not prevent a halt. The collisions, the race and the alignment of the gaps are simulated, not proved.

summary: Word map phi twice per counter step and the anomaly proved in Lean for all parameters; the word-and-gap pattern alone is not invariant (a short Q configuration halts, Lean); non-halting hinges on a race between the word and the collision cascade; open. Added 12 Nov: 29 more Lean rules (this machine's one-unit anomaly, some collisions) and a partial macro map; 187 of 236 simulated collisions follow a proved rule.
